question.worked_solution:
First, let's calculate ${x}^{5}\cdot q(x):$

$$
{x}^{5}\cdot q(x)={x}^{5}\cdot (4x)=4{x}^{6}.
$$

When we divide the two functions $p(x)$ and ${x}^{5}\cdot q(x),$ we get a constant, and the limit of a constant is just the constant itself:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to -\infty }\frac{p(x)}{{x}^{5}\cdot q(x)} & ={lim}_{x\to -\infty }\frac{3{x}^{6}}{4{x}^{6}} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to -\infty }\frac{3}{4} \\  & =\frac{3}{4}\end{aligned}
$$
